28eb33dc.task: Who is the CEO of the parent company of the airline with the most domestic routes in the United States?
28eb33dc.label: fail
28eb33dc.notes: Diagnosed from the full trace: the agent issued 6 LLM calls and 6 searches, and every single one resulted in another tool call -- it never once decided to commit to an answer. All 5 search queries were near-duplicates of each other ('airline with most domestic routes', 'which US airline operates the most domestic routes 2024 2025', 'Southwest vs American vs United domestic routes', etc.). Root cause: the specific metric requested ('number of domestic routes per airline') isn't a commonly published stat -- every source returned a different proxy (busiest routes by revenue, by seat capacity, market share %) and the agent kept grinding for the exact metric instead of settling for a proxy with a caveat. It also burned its entire step budget on hop 1 of a 2-hop question and never attempted to find the CEO at all. Contrast with run ba364990 (tallest building), which handled similar ambiguity well by presenting multiple interpretations instead of endlessly searching. Fix applied: added a system prompt instructing the agent to (a) budget steps across multi-hop sub-questions, (b) give a best-effort answer with an explicit caveat after 2-3 failed attempts at an exact metric rather than reformulating indefinitely, and (c) check source recency before treating something as 'latest'. Also raised max_steps from 6 to 8. Re-run this exact question after the fix to see if it now either succeeds or fails gracefully with a caveat instead of MAX_STEPS_REACHED.

ba364990.task: What is the tallest building in the city that hosted the most recent Summer Olympics?
ba364990.label: pass
ba364990.notes: Handled genuine ambiguity (tallest structure vs. tallest habitable building) by presenting both interpretations instead of confidently picking one -- arguably the correct behavior for a question this ambiguous. Good test case later for whether the judge should reward this kind of hedging or penalize it for not committing to one answer.
